name: File Upload Component
description: A file upload that works by keyboard, pointer, touch, and drag and drop: a Choose files button opens the picker, the whole area takes dropped files without the browser opening them, each file is checked, listed by name with its own progress and buttons, and announced once, and the server checks everything again.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Let people attach files by keyboard, pointer, touch, or drag and drop. A Choose files button opens the picker; the whole upload area takes dropped files, and a file dropped elsewhere on the page doesn't open in the tab. Check each file's type, size, and count in the browser for convenience, and on the server for real; list each file by name with its status, progress, and buttons named after it; and announce changes through one status region. Build on the project's upload component, library, or service when it has one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A Choose files button that opens the picker, so nothing needs dragging (WCAG 2.2 2.5.7)
The whole area takes dropped files, with a highlight that doesn't flicker and shows only for file drags
A file dropped elsewhere on the page doesn't open in the tab
The input cleared after each choice, so the same file can be chosen again
Checks against accept by type and extension in any case, size, and count, with the server checking again
A list of files by name with status, a named progress element, and Remove, Retry, and Cancel named after each file
One status region for added, removed, uploaded, and failed files
Uploads that can be cancelled, and retried without a second copy
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection), plus any upload component, library, or service the project already uses. Build on them, and keep their APIs and upload code.
2. Choose what the task needs: one file or several, previews, uploading as files are added or with the form, paste. Leave out the rest.
3. Build the area as in frameworkPatterns.uploadMarkup: a group named by the field's label, the hint, the error, Choose files, the hidden file input, the list, and the status region.
4. Wire choosing and dropping as in frameworkPatterns.chooseAndDrop.
5. Check each file as in frameworkPatterns.fileCheck, and show rejections by name.
6. List the files and upload them (implementationDetails.fileList, implementationDetails.uploads), with focus kept after Remove.
7. Make sure the server checks the type by content, the size, and the count again.
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a touch screen, and real drag and drop, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Let anyone attach the right files, see what happens to each, and fix what's wrong, whether they use a keyboard, a pointer, a touch screen, or drag files from their desktop.

anatomy.hierarchy: The group holds the label, the hint, the field's error, Choose files, the hidden file input, the list of files, and the status region. The whole group is the drop area.

slotNotes.group: An element with role="group", named by the field's visible label (aria-labelledby). It isn't a button: interactive elements can't sit inside a button, and the drop area is a region, not a control.
slotNotes.hint: What's accepted and the limits ("PDF or Word files, up to 10 MB each"), and that files can be dropped or chosen; connected to Choose files with aria-describedby.
slotNotes.error: For the field as a whole, such as "Choose at least one file", in Choose files' aria-describedby; empty and hidden until needed.
slotNotes.chooseButton: A <button type="button"> that opens the picker by calling the hidden input's click(). It's the way in that needs no dragging (WCAG 2.2 2.5.7).
slotNotes.fileInput: type="file" with accept and multiple, hidden; accept filters the picker. The app keeps the chosen files and sends them.
slotNotes.fileItem: The file's name as text, never HTML, its size, its status, its progress while uploading, and its buttons.
slotNotes.progress: The native <progress> element, named after its file ("Uploading report.pdf").
slotNotes.removeButton: Named after its file: visible "Remove" plus visually hidden text with the name ("Remove report.pdf"). Retry and Cancel are named the same way.
slotNotes.status: One status region, present before it changes, for files added, removed, rejected, uploaded, and failed.

files.description: The chosen files, each with an id (crypto.randomUUID()), the File, its status (ready, uploading, uploaded, failed, cancelled, unknown), its progress, and its error.

dragging.description: Whether files are being dragged over the area; kept steady by a counter of dragenter and dragleave events.

multiple.description: Whether several files can be chosen; with one, a new file replaces the current one.

accept.description: The accepted extensions and types, such as ".pdf,.doc,.docx" or "image/*", for the picker and the checks.

maxSizeBytes.description: The size limit per file (10 MB suggested).

maxFiles.description: How many files can be chosen.

error.description: The field's error, such as "Choose at least one file".

interactions.accessibilityNotes: A click, Enter, or Space on Choose files calls the hidden input's click().
After reading the files, clear the input's value: otherwise choosing the same file again fires no change in Chrome and Safari. Focus stays on Choose files.
A counter of dragenter and dragleave events keeps the highlight steady while the pointer crosses elements inside the area. Drags of text or links don't highlight it.

interactions.when: the drag carries files and misses the area
interactions.accessibilityNotes: While the uploader is on the page, cancel dragover and drop for files on the whole page, so a near miss doesn't open the file in the tab and replace the page.
Focus moves to the next file's Remove button, or the previous one, or Choose files when the list is empty; never to the page body.
The retry sends the file's id again, so the server keeps one copy if the first upload reached it.

responsiveBehavior.layout: The area fills its container and is at least 96 px tall (suggested); it has no breakpoints of its own.
responsiveBehavior.phones: The list is one column, with each file's buttons at the end of its row; thumbnails are optional. Buttons are at least 44 by 44 px on touch (suggested).
responsiveBehavior.reflow: At 320 px wide, long file names wrap, and nothing scrolls sideways.

variants.singleFile: One file: a new choice replaces the current one, and the status region says so.
variants.multipleFiles: Several files, up to maxFiles; the status region says when the limit is reached.
variants.withPreview: Optional image previews in an from URL.createObjectURL(), released with URL.revokeObjectURL() when the file is removed. An doesn't run an SVG's scripts; a user's file never goes in an
variants.uploadOnAdd: Each file uploads as it's added, with its own progress, Cancel, and Retry.
variants.uploadWithForm: The files are sent with the form; the app adds them to the form data, since the input is cleared after each choice.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing moves; the progress element still fills.

requirements.1.3.1: The group is named by the field's label, and the hint and the error describe Choose files.
requirements.1.4.3: The area's text, file names, and messages meet 4.5:1.
requirements.1.4.11: The area's edge, the highlight, and the focus indicator meet 3:1.
requirements.2.1.1: Choosing, removing, retrying, and cancelling all work from the keyboard.
requirements.2.4.3: After Remove, focus lands on another file's button or on Choose files.
requirements.2.5.7: Choose files is the way in that needs no dragging.
requirements.2.5.8: Buttons are at least 24 by 24 px.
requirements.3.3.1: Rejected files say why, by name, in text.
requirements.4.1.2: Each progress element and button is named after its file.
requirements.4.1.3: Added, removed, rejected, uploaded, and failed files are announced through one status region.

keyboardNavigation.choose: Tab to Choose files; Enter or Space opens the picker.
keyboardNavigation.fileButtons: Tab moves through each file's buttons. File rows aren't focusable, and there are no row shortcuts: Delete or Backspace on a row would need a Tab stop per file, and the Remove button is enough.

chooseButton.aria-describedby: The hint and the field's error

removeButton.name: Visible "Remove" plus visually hidden text with the file name

screenReader.added: "2 files added: report.pdf, notes.docx", and rejections by name with the reason.
screenReader.progress: Meaningful moments only, such as "report.pdf uploaded"; never every percent.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

uploadMarkup.description: The upload area: a group named by the label, the hint and the error on Choose files, the hidden file input, a file in the list with its named progress and Remove button, and the status region.
uploadMarkup.html:
Documents (optional)

PDF or Word files, up to 10 MB each. Drop them here, or choose them.

  • report.pdf

chooseAndDrop.description: Choosing and dropping files: Choose files opens the picker, the input is cleared after each choice, a counter keeps the highlight steady, and the page doesn't open a file dropped elsewhere.

fileCheck.description: Why a file can't be added: its type against accept, by extension in any case and by type, its size, and the count. The server checks again.

implementationDetails.checks: Check each file when it's added (frameworkPatterns.fileCheck). Reject it next to its name with the reason ("photo.heic isn't a PDF or Word file", "video.mp4 is larger than 10 MB"), and say it in the status region. file.type is the browser's guess from the extension, and empty for types it doesn't know, so match accept against the extension too, ignoring case. These checks are for the person's convenience: the server checks the type by the file's content, the size, and the count again, and treats file names as text.
implementationDetails.duplicates: A file with the same name, size, and modification time as one already chosen is ignored with a message, or replaces it; say which.
implementationDetails.fileList: Each file shows its name, size, and status: ready, uploading, uploaded, failed, cancelled, or unknown. Its buttons are Remove, and Cancel or Retry while they apply, each named after the file. The status region says when a file is added, removed, uploaded, or fails, at meaningful moments, not every percent.
implementationDetails.uploads: fetch() reports no upload progress, so progress needs XMLHttpRequest's upload events, or the project's upload library. Cancel aborts the request. Give each file an id (crypto.randomUUID()); a dropped connection leaves the outcome unknown, since the server may have the file, so the status says so, and Retry sends the same id, so the server keeps one copy.
implementationDetails.paste: Optional: files pasted into the area go through the same checks.
implementationDetails.reset: A form reset doesn't clear the app's list of chosen files, since the input is empty after each choice anyway. After a reset that wasn't cancelled, clear the list, cancel unfinished uploads, release preview URLs, and say so in the status region. The form's reset event comes first, and a later listener can still cancel the reset, so wait for the event to finish and check defaultPrevented.

edgeCases.longNames: Long file names wrap, or are shortened in the middle with the full name kept in the item's text for screen readers.
edgeCases.manyFiles: The status region says when the limit is reached; with many files, a summary such as "8 of 10 files uploaded".
edgeCases.leavingDuringUpload: While uploads run, warn before the page is left (beforeunload), or let them finish in the background if the app can.
edgeCases.required: A required upload says so in words; a submit without a file shows the field's error, and focus moves to Choose files.
edgeCases.disabled: When the upload can't be used yet, say why in text, and give Choose files aria-disabled="true" so it can still be found.
edgeCases.serverRejects: A file the server rejects shows its message next to the file, with Remove.

must: Build on the project's upload component, library, or service when it has one, and keep its API
Offer Choose files as the way in that needs no dragging
Check files on the server again, and show file names as text
Name each file's buttons and progress after the file
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add an upload or drag-and-drop library without asking
Make the drop area a button, or put buttons inside one
Trust the browser's type or size checks, or insert file names as HTML
Show a user's file in an <iframe> or <object>
Announce every percent of an upload
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Choose files opens the picker with a click, Enter, or Space, so nothing needs dragging
Files dropped anywhere in the area are added, and a file dropped elsewhere on the page doesn't open in the tab
The highlight shows only while files are dragged over the area, and doesn't flicker over the elements inside it
The same file can be chosen again after it was removed
Each file is checked against the accepted types, with extensions in any case, the size, and the count, and a rejected file says why, by name
The server checks the type by content, the size, and the count again, and file names are shown as text
Each file's Remove, Retry, and Cancel buttons are named after it, and its progress is a progress element named after it
One status region announces files added, removed, uploaded, and failed, without announcing every percent
After Remove, focus lands on another file's Remove button or on Choose files, never on the page body
A dropped connection shows the upload's outcome as unknown, and Retry doesn't create a second copy
A form reset clears the list of chosen files and cancels unfinished uploads, and a cancelled reset changes nothing
The area's edge, its text, and the focus indicator meet the contrast minimums, and buttons are at least 24 by 24 px
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens, like its other form controls
